results.title: Field Data Collection - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
results.content: Field data collection is defined as the process of gathering spatial and non-spatial data in real-time using mobile GIS technologies, which enhances the efficiency and quality of data through features like digital editing, remote access to shared datasets, and immediate updates during field surveys. Pervasive computing systems (PeCS) often require time series observations of users and their collective behavior, including social interactions across multiple devices and locations, resulting in complex structured sensor data that may not be compatible with traditional data collection methods. Traditional field mapping tasks using desktop GIS software are time consuming, and the quality of data collected by those methods is difficult to control; semantic integrity is a separate issue that can be addressed by integrating GPS, GIS, and remote sensing capabilities into mobile GIS services with semantic plausibility control, enabling field workers to edit, update, and validate both spatial and nonspatial data, improving efficiency and location quality in field data collection.
